newsitem.title: CANADA: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 18.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - August 18.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

TORONTO - Canada's Molson's Brewery produces television commercial with overtly homosexual theme, but says it is not sure whether the 30-second spot featuring two women kissing in a bar is going to be aired on prime time.

BONN - Phone companies are attracting thousands of Europeans used to paying some of the world's highest phone bills with projects which offer customers free calls if they listen to advertising spots before and at regular intervals during their conversation.

LONDON - Safeway Plc, the British supermarket group, is launching a 20-million-pound ($32.2-million) advertising campaign that promises to give customers products for free if they can find them cheaper at any major competitor stores.
LONDON - FCA! advertising agency says its recent merger with a UK-based branding specialist will help it grow across Europe and satisfy growing client demand for "through-the-line" service.

CHICAGO - Familiar advertising themes and jingles, some mothballed for more than two decades, are making a comeback this year as marketers attempt to cash in on long-established brand equities by conjuring up warm and fuzzy images from the past.
NEW YORK - Sprint Corp. will announce this week that it is the sole sponsor of an upcoming concert tour by the Rolling Stones, according to a source close to the deal.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BERLIN - A Berlin court sides with Deutsche Telekom AG and prevents six private television stations from broadcasting over the company's cable system in the area of Germany's largest city.
LONDON - The launch of digital satellite services in 1998 will put a brake on BSkyB's profit growth although details of costs and revenue drivers are still sketchy, analysts say.

MEXICO CITY - TV Azteca, Mexico's second largest broadcaster, will invest some $200 million over the next three years in expanding local stations, acquiring more stations in Central and South America and boosting the export of programming, says president Ricardo Salinas Pliego. TV Azteca's initial public offering last week was one of Mexico's largest in recent years.

SYDNEY - Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd is expected to report this week that movie flops "Speed II" and "Volcano" held back the global media group from achieving Murdoch's own 20-percent profit growth forecast for 1996/97. *******

MADRID - Spanish pay television group Sogecable reaches a deal with Universal Studios over film and "pay per view" rights and a new action-suspense channel, which will allow it to broadcast Universal films on pay-TV channel Canal Plus.

LONDON - Moves by the UK's TV watchdog to prevent BSkyB Plc from selling television channels in packages or bundles could spell the end for some small channels, according to BSkyB Chief Executive Sam Chisholm.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

SHANGHAI - The Coca-Cola Company launches a new fizzy soft drink called Smart that it says is the first carbonated drink designed by an international company specifically for the enormous youth market in China.
NEW YORK - Ford Motor Co plans to unveil a new "sporty" luxury sedan in 1999 for its Lincoln unit, the Wall Street Journal reports.

LONDON - Britain's supermarkets, faced with tight competition in groceries, are stepping further into other retail sectors, with banking, insurance and even dry cleaning services just the latest areas on their shopping list.

NEW YORK - International Business Machines Corp will unveil a computer family designed to conduct a wide range of business operations on the Internet this week. IBM expects the line will spark new life into its hardware business.

NEW YORK - Hotel companies are seeing business surging and their investors are seeing stock prices rising, according to a report in Barron's. Occupancy rates are now at 65 percent nationally and rising room rates have increased revenues per room, says the paper.
NEW YORK - Netscape Communications Corp will introduce a stand-alone version of Navigator, its popular Internet-browser software, the Wall Street Journal reports, citing sources close to the project.

FRANKFURT - Earnings growth at BMW AG, the German car company, should continue in the second half of 1997 at the pace of the first six months but the the strong pound is hurting earnings at UK unit Rover, says the company's chief executive.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LOS ANGELES - Hundreds of caped "vampires" are celebrating the 100th anniversary of the publication of the novel "Dracula" at the "Dracula '97" convention, where Gothic-style clothing is available at prices ranging from $250 to $1,000, Dracula T-shirts cost $20, and for $290 one can pick up a coffin-shaped book shelf. "Lord of the Fangs" is doing a brisk business at his booth fitting people with long sharp teeth.

TAIPEI - A Hong Kong-based company, I-Quest, is liberating globe-trotting executives from their laptop computers by equipping hotel rooms with feature-packed, Internet-linked computers running a palette of business, network and information software in a package they call WorldRoom at a flat cost to the guest or hotel of US$20 a day. I-Quest is aiming at 170,000 rooms at 2,500 Pacific Rim hotels.

WELLINGTON - Neil Harrap's "Fly by Wire" invention, the first adventure ride offering full pilot control of a high-speed tethered plane, is attracting the interest of foreign companies, including theme park operators and hoteliers who want to buy the system. The ride, which reaches speeds of 120kmh (75mph), is as close as most people will come to flying a fighter jet.
